sessionTitle: Data Science & Machine Learning with Microsoft Fabric

announcements.name: Diabetes-projection demo using a public Microsoft dataset [00:05:00]
announcements.shortDescription: A healthcare scenario ingests data from Azure Blob storage, splits it 70/30 for training and validation, and compares a linear regression against a decision tree regressor, with the decision tree scoring better
announcements.longDescription: The presenter lists and retrieves machine learning experiments in a Fabric workspace, focusing on one named 'experiment-diabetes', and retrieves its runs (each with a run ID, finished status, and artifact URL). A quick visualization compares models, showing better scores with the decision tree regressor than with linear regression. The presenter explains that you can run multiple experiment iterations, inspect per-run metrics like training score and mean square error, then select a preferred run and save it as a model in the Fabric workspace (named 'build table 2602' [inferred]).

announcements.name: Fabric Data Agent for natural-language insights [00:14:49]
announcements.shortDescription: Any user can point a generative-AI-backed agent at OneLake data, add custom instructions, and receive insights; it is currently read-only
announcements.longDescription: The Fabric Data Agent lets anyone—not just data scientists or ML engineers—get insights from data, using generative AI behind the scenes. As long as the data is in OneLake, users can add it to the data agent, supply custom instructions, and receive insights. A current main limitation is that it is read-only: it can return insights from the data but cannot write back. Once ready, the agent can be consumed in Fabric, on the Foundry side, integrated with Copilot Studio, exposed as an MCP server, and deployed into Microsoft 365 Copilot [inferred].
